exemptions.project|len(WIDE) == 41|#0: fixture premise, not a claim about the tool: it pins the width arithmetic the other cases depend on. The s288 precedent for premise assertions.
exemptions.test_reflow_tags_an_overlong_anchor_and_: OVER-DETERMINED. A tag that fails to resolve is caught by the tool's own post-write resolution check, which restores and returns 2 — so every single-subject mutation reddens the exit-code assertion first. This assertion is the positive control that the self-check ran on the committed result.

OVER-DETERMINED by _overwide: a tree left over-wide is refused and restored before this line is reached, reddening the exit-code assertion first. Reddening it alone would need a two-subject mutation (skip the format AND the width check), which the one-probe-one-assertion rule forbids.

OVER-DETERMINED, same mechanism as `widest <= 60`: a run that never reflowed leaves the line over-wide, which _overwide catches first. It is kept as the positive control that the fixture really did overrun — without it a fixture that quietly stopped overrunning would satisfy the whole test.
